brief: August employment data confirm TS Lombard's view that recent weakness was noise. Growth ran above trend early in the year, seasonal factors pulled it below trend, and August corrects that with upward revisions to July, preserving the uptrend. The NFIB survey, a reliable employment lead, points to a pick-up. A soft patch remains a risk as the consumer shifts from Q1 tax refunds and a Q2 savings rate decline onto employment and wage growth, a transition today's data confirm, driven by broadening earnings growth. The market needs proof Warsh can hike, so TS Lombard expects a hike this month, since failing would leave him with a credibility mess. The market is pricing this as a one time credibility hike, a framing TS Lombard ties to European central banking rather than the more inflation prone, flexible US labour market, where ULC growth is artificially low from last year's uncertainty driven hiring freeze and wage growth is rising once low signal sectors are stripped out. This view is untested and most FOMC members do not share it, so Warsh may need to justify hiking again later. FX's muted reaction to today's data supports TS Lombard's read that the hike is merely reactionary.
